payload.task: Li-ion self_diffusion (cm2/s) in pristine crystalline LiF by molecular dynamics
payload.reason: Premise check failed: the quantity is not measurable with MD for a pristine (defect-free) LiF crystal. Li transport in rocksalt LiF is vacancy-mediated. A perfect periodic cell contains no vacancies, and thermally creating one (Schottky pair, formation enthalpy roughly 2.3-2.7 eV in the literature) is a rare event that will essentially never happen in a ~10^3-atom cell over ns. Without vacancies, Li ions only vibrate, the MSD plateaus, and D = 0 within noise. That zero is an artifact of the missing defects, not a material property. Order-of-magnitude intrinsic estimate, D ~ a^2*nu*exp(-H_S/2kT)*exp(-E_m/kT) with a^2*nu ~ 8e-3 cm2/s, H_S ~ 2.4 eV, E_m ~ 0.7 eV: about 1e-34 cm2/s at 300 K and about 1e-11 cm2/s near the melting point (~1120 K). The MD detection limit is roughly 1e-9 cm2/s (~1 A^2 MSD over ~10 ns), so the gap is about 25 orders of magnitude at 300 K and still about 2 near melting. At 1100 K the expected equilibrium number of vacancies in a 1000-atom cell is about 0.003. Superheating the crystal until Li moves would measure melting or defect nucleation, not crystalline diffusion. Also, Li diffusion measured in real LiF below roughly 800 K is extrinsic (set by aliovalent impurities), so 'pristine' has no single experimental value to validate against. /data/calibration/tier1.json has no LiF records. No independent known result can be recovered with this setup, so no number is reported.

details.premise_check: fail: below MD detection limit by about 2 to 25 orders of magnitude depending on T; defect concentration in a pristine cell is undefined/zero on MD timescales
details.estimate_inputs_are_approximate: H_S ~2.4 eV and E_m ~0.7 eV are typical literature magnitudes for LiF, used only for an order-of-magnitude feasibility argument and not reported as results
well_posed_alternatives: Li-vacancy migration barrier E_m by NEB with an MLIP (e.g. MACE-MP), validated against a DFT NEB on the same cell

MD with an explicit, stated defect content (one Li vacancy, or one charge-neutral Schottky pair) at 800-1100 K in NVT, reporting vacancy diffusivity and D_Li conditional on that vacancy fraction, plus an Arrhenius E_m. Multiple seeds and block averaging give the uncertainty
Self-diffusion of Li in molten LiF above ~1121 K, which is well-posed in MD and can be validated against measured molten-salt data or, first, recovering a known melt property such as density
